cards.topic: Movement into and out of cells
cards.back: The **net movement of water molecules** from a region of **higher water potential** to a region of **lower water potential**, through a **partially permeable membrane**.

cards.topic: Movement into and out of cells
cards.front: What is the water potential of pure water? What happens when solute is added?
cards.back:
Pure water has the **highest** water potential: **0 kPa**.
Adding solute makes the water potential **more negative** (lower).

cards.topic: Movement into and out of cells
cards.back: The movement of molecules or ions **against their concentration gradient**, using **energy from ATP**, through **carrier proteins** in the membrane.
The **maximum rate** of an enzyme-catalysed reaction, reached when **all the active sites are occupied** by substrate.

cards.front: What is the Michaelis–Menten constant, $K_\text{m}$? What does a low value mean?
cards.back:
The **substrate concentration** at which the rate is **half of $V_\text{max}$**.
A **low $K_\text{m}$** means the enzyme has a **high affinity** for its substrate.

cards.front: How does a competitive inhibitor affect $V_\text{max}$ and $K_\text{m}$?
cards.back:
It has a similar shape to the substrate and **binds to the active site**.
$V_\text{max}$ is **unchanged** (it can still be reached at high substrate concentration), but $K_\text{m}$ **increases**.
Each new DNA molecule contains **one original (parental) strand** and **one newly synthesised strand**.
A **sequence of nucleotides** that forms part of a DNA molecule and **codes for a polypeptide**.

cards.front: Define a gene mutation and name three types.
cards.back:
A **change in the sequence of nucleotides (bases)** in DNA.
Types: **substitution**, **deletion** and **insertion**.

cards.front: Mitosis produces what kind of cells? Give four reasons it is important.
cards.back:
**Genetically identical** daughter cells.
Used for **growth**, **repair** of damaged tissue, **replacement** of cells and **asexual reproduction**. Also **clonal expansion** of lymphocytes.
